comparison: Both evaluations agree that the crystal structures of PL35 family enzymes (C2-C4, C30-C32) are well-supported. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on crystallographic data quality, and peer reviewers acknowledge successful structure determination as a strength with no concerns raised about structural data quality.

Complete agreement on claims C33-C36 regarding Mn2+ cofactor role. Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewer initially questioned ICP-MS data presentation but after revision accepted the evidence. Both acknowledge the convergence of structural, ICP-MS, and mutagenesis data supporting Mn2+ as critical cofactor.

Significant disagreement on structural similarity to alginate lyases (C5, C37-C42, C62). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on DALI Z-scores and RMSD values, but peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning the DALI methodology and suggesting local rather than global alignment. Peer reviewer notes authors did not adequately address concerns about evolutionary conclusions.

Complete agreement on catalytic residue identification (C43-C45, C64). Both rate as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers acknowledge comprehensive mutagenesis campaign as a strength, and both accept that complete loss of activity upon mutation strongly supports the catalytic mechanism.

Both evaluations rate claims C46-C47, C65-C66 about substrate binding cavity as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes the causal link between cavity dimensions and promiscuity is speculative without co-crystal structures. Peer reviewers similarly note the explanation is lacking and the study is incomplete without enzyme-substrate complex structures.

Both evaluations rate docking-based mechanistic claims (C48-C50, C57-C60, plus C55-C56 in peer review) as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes mechanistic details are inferred from docking rather than direct observation. Peer reviewers emphasize over-reliance on molecular docking, lack of MD analysis, and absence of experimental enzyme-substrate complex structures.

Partial disagreement on His188 role in alginate activity (C51-C52, C61). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting His188 is necessary but not sufficient. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, pointing out that His188 also affects HS activity, suggesting the specificity claim is overstated and the mechanistic interpretation incomplete.

Both address the negative result that single mutation cannot transfer alginate activity (C53, C71). OpenEval includes this in SUPPORTED evaluation noting it appropriately tempers conclusions. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, accepting this demonstrates complexity of substrate specificity determinants beyond single residues.

Both evaluations agree on substrate preference explanation (C67-C68, C54 in peer review). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on comparison with bifunctional lyases and established knowledge about anti-base His role. Peer reviewers accept this interpretation without challenge, consistent with mechanistic understanding from other lyases.

Complete agreement on background claims (C1, C25-C27). Both rate as SUPPORTED, acknowledging these are established findings from previous work (Wei et al., 2024) that provide context for the structural study. Both accept the substrate specificity patterns as established background knowledge.

Partial overlap on substrate specificity claims. OpenEval addresses C54-C56 (docking-based selectivity) as UNCERTAIN. Peer review addresses C54, C67-C68 (substrate preference for GlcUA) as SUPPORTED based on experimental data and established mechanistic knowledge. The evaluations address different aspects of substrate specificity.

Both address evolutionary hypothesis (C6, C42, C62) but with different emphasis. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting structural similarity is compelling but phylogenetic analysis needed. Peer reviewer also rates as UNCERTAIN but focuses more on methodological concerns about structural alignment approach (DALI vs. local alignment).

OpenEval evaluates nomenclature proposal (C72-C75) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is speculative and primarily a discussion point. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing these specific claims about Hepar_II_III module distribution and naming.

OpenEval evaluates background knowledge claims (C7-C24) about GAGs, alginate, and lyases as SUPPORTED, noting these are established facts with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing these background context claims.
